title: This Deep-Sea Crab Waves Its Claws to Grow Its Own Food
subject: yeti crab

scenes.text: A crab waves its hairy claws for hours. It's not saying hello.
It's a yeti crab, about nine centimeters long, living near methane seeps off Costa Rica.
Its claws and body are covered in hair-like bristles. And on those bristles, bacteria grow.
The bacteria live on gases from the seep. Waving stirs the water, bringing them fresh oxygen and sulfide.
Then the crab combs the bacteria off with its mouthparts and eats them.

description:
The yeti crab Kiwa puravida waves its bristly claws over methane seeps off Costa Rica.
Bacteria grow on its bristles and the crab eats them. The waving likely brings the bacteria fresh oxygen and sulfide.
What would you farm if you lived in the deep sea?
first_comment: Farmer crab or hairy monster? Which is cooler?
